To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
spider toxins target voltage-gated sodium channels with high selectivity and potency.
Spider toxins target a wide range of Nav channel subtypes, but with a high degree of specificity.
spider neurotoxins represent a diverse family of toxins targeting the voltage gated sodium channel and that their action on channel activation and/or inactivation is complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification and characterization of the pharmacophores of spider toxins, their binding sites, and mode of action on voltage gated sodium channels, with the aim of understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying these actions.
the characterization and functional analysis of the molecular determinants of the interaction of these spider toxins with Nav channels, and with the development of new tools to target these channels.
the identification of spider toxins as tools to define novel molecular mechanisms of action, to develop biopesticides, and to target specific ion channel subtypes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we are still in the early stages of understanding the molecular mechanisms of spider toxins targeting Nav channels.
the field of spider neurotoxins has been greatly advanced by the isolation of new toxins and the determination of their pharmacophores.
the study of spider toxins is in its infancy and that the potential for the development of novel drugs, insecticides and tools to study ion channels has yet to be fully realized.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
spider neurotoxins are highly potent, specific, and versatile tools to define and modulate Nav channel function.
the spider toxins have been a rich source of novel molecular probes for the study of Nav channels, and that they have the potential to become important drugs, insecticides or biopesticides.
the spider toxins are highly potent and specific ligands that target Nav channels and other ion channels.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Nav channel represents a complex target for a number toxins that interact with a variety of binding sites and that these toxins are likely to represent a rich source of novel tools for the study of this important ion channel.
spider toxins are a rich source of novel pharmacophores that target Nav channels and that these toxins can be used to delineate novel molecular determinants of Nav channel function.
spider toxins are highly specific ligands for voltage gated sodium channels.
